focus: `.opencode/hooks/goal/` in full: slice module, core, four adapters, manage CLI, six test suites
novelty: First ring: the engine had not been read anywhere in this lineage. 14 paths, four contradiction classes, one dead-code duplicate, one unreachable diagnostics path.

label: The live operator flag file documents SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED, which exists nowhere else and disables nothing
detail: Canonical name is OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED; aliases are OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED, MK_GOAL_DISABLED, MK_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED. SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED is in neither list and appears exactly once in the repository. Every neighbouring line in the live file uses the SYSTEM_<CONCERN>_DISABLED shape, which genuinely works for dispatch (hook-flags.cjs:53), so the one line that breaks the pattern is the one that does nothing. The file is gitignored, so no test can catch it.
novelty: unreported; found by reading the live file, not the example

label: The PLUGIN_DISABLED error names the alias, not the switch that fired
detail: DISABLED_ENV is OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED and is interpolated into eleven guard messages, but every guard calls isPluginDisabled() which reads OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED first. Setting the canonical flag produces a message naming a different variable.

label: The kill switch also switches off the session-free reads and the aggregate diagnostics
detail: The CLI returns PLUGIN_DISABLED before routing, so packet, packet-log, doctor and health all fail while disabled, though the docs describe them as session-free and read-only. Meanwhile the library functions appendPacketLog (goal-core.cjs:1113) and describePacketGoal (goal-core.cjs:1042) carry no disable check, so a direct importer still writes rows that the CLI refuses to write.
novelty: the asymmetry between the CLI and the library on the same flag is unreported

label: The hook enforces the durable budget on the packets the contract excludes
detail: The manifest says appliesTo is phase parents and top-level packets, with phase children unbounded. resolveGoalBudget reads only warnChars and errorChars and drops appliesTo; budgetState compares every packet; the CLI emits warning= for a phase child that is over. Re-tested in ring 3 against the validator's own resolver.
novelty: unreported crossing of the hook and the spec-kit contract

label: Injection-only does not mean read-only: both injection-only adapters mutate the record
detail: Cursor and Devin both import recordTurn and bump turnsUsed, revision, updatedAtMs and lastActivityAtMs. goal-plugin.md states this precisely; README.md's injection-only framing does not.
novelty: precision gap between the two engine docs

label: The manage CLI and the OpenCode plugin do not expose the same status field names
detail: The plugin contract names tokens_used and usage_source as canonical, with budget-prefixed aliases. The CLI emits usage_source but never tokens_used, so a script reading the canonical field works against one surface and silently gets nothing from the other.

label: resolveWorkspaceRoot is a byte-for-byte twin of resolveRepoRoot and has no consumer
detail: Same markers, same depth loop, same fallback. The core calls its own resolveRepoRoot at four sites; resolveWorkspaceRoot is referenced only by its definition, its export and one test. goal-slice.cjs has three importers: goal-core.cjs, opencode-goal.js and its own test.

label: README section 6 omits OPENCODE_GOAL_RUNTIME_LABEL, and its name collides conceptually with --runtime
detail: The CLI reads the label; the repo-root example env documents it; the engine README does not. --runtime is constrained to lowercase and forms the state key, while the label is a free-form display string carrying values like Pi and Cursor.

label: The append gateway could not be used inside a contained lineage
detail: append-mode-event.cjs writes the state log and receipts under the spec folder, outside this lineage's bound write surface. Records are appended in-lineage in the same field shape instead. Recorded as a deviation in every iteration file and in research.md.
novelty: lineage-local; a general finding for the fan-out harness, not for the goal engine
